Something Very Fishy About the Way the Linux Foundation Puts Its Leadership 'on Sale'

I'm trying slowly to create an alternative. I don't think it will be an alternative desktop in this decade but may change the game for the social structure of OS development.

The idea is to have people structure code in a way where multiple semi-independent project can be fed into a compiler based on a manifest file. That then builds the OS. This would completely remove any centralization.

Linux, being coded in c, is all coded in a single namespace, with thousands of people working on it, and it is more dynamic than most projects built in an object oriented language. Encapsulation and object orientation are over rated. So why not just make a c compiler that instead of complaining when it sees two versions of a declaration, just applies the preferable one according the the manifest.

Then you can simply link to git repositories, and for a project to override the behavior of a function it just has to declare it. It's sort of like cascading style sheets.

From that you could easily build small single purpose operating systems just by over riding some placeholder function while the really complex stuff needed to get an OS booted remains the same.

By lowering the bar for making simple operating systems it then snowballs into full fledged operating systems, all without a single character needed to operate a foundation.
